title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the previous pages). Grothendieck uses a finite model of the moduli stack: E' ≅ U_{0,3}/S_3 is the j-line, with S_3 acting on the λ-line U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. M'_{1,1} is modelled as [U_{0,3}/S_3] and M_{1,1} as [U_{0,3}/S̃_3]. Here S̃_3 is a central extension of S_3 by μ = Z/2 = {±1}, acting through S_3. It is the quotient of SL(2,Z) by a normal free subgroup of rank 2 inside Γ(2) (the next page notes S^{+} ≅ SL(2,Z)). The point o ∈ E'(Q) is j = 0. Its fibre in U_{0,3} is the S_3-orbit {−ρ, −ρ²}, with stabiliser Z/3. Over Q this fibre is Spec Q(j), where j here is a cube root of unity, so Q(j) = Q(√−3). This defines a μ-torsor P_0 on which S_3 acts through the sign map sg: S_3 → μ.

This page.
(1) Diagram (31): S̃_3 --can--> S_3 --sg--> μ, together with Γ_Q → μ, the quadratic character of Q(√−3).
(2) NB: the kernel of S̃_3 → μ is an extension of Z/3 by Z/2. Such an extension is split and abelian, so the kernel is Z/6, generated by a lift of ρ.
(3) The category of lifts of the rational point o of E' to rational points of M'_{1,1} (resp. M_{1,1}) is equivalent to the category of S_3-torsors P (resp. S̃_3-torsors P̃) over Q that lift P_0.
(4) The previously chosen lift T comes from the section μ ≅ {1, σ_0} ⊂ S_3. T admits no lift T̃: a transposition lifts to an element of order 4 in S̃_3, and Q(√−3) does not embed in a cyclic quartic field.
(5) Hence isomorphism classes of points of M'_{1,1} (resp. M_{1,1}) over o are the classes of lifts of Γ_Q → μ to Γ_Q → S_3 (resp. S̃_3), up to conjugation by the kernels S_3' = Z/3 (resp. S̃_3' = Z/6).
(6) The page begins classifying lifts Γ_Q → S_3 by their image. The next page concludes: the image is either a transposition subgroup, which cannot lift, or all of S_3. So one must look for surjections onto S_3, i.e. dihedral S_3-fields with quadratic resolvent Q(√−3), in other words Kummer fields Q(ζ_3, ∛m). Whether these lift to S̃_3 is declared a 'pleasant class field theory exercise' and set aside.

Purpose: to compare rational points of the stacks with sections or splittings of the arithmetic fundamental group extension 1 → SL(2,Z)^ → π_1(M_{1,1}) → Γ_Q → 1. This is an instance of the section conjecture for orbifold points with nontrivial automorphisms, i.e. points 'at infinity of the stack'.
errors: The 'exercise' has a definite answer inside the stated model. S̃_3 with elements of order 4 lifting transpositions is the binary dihedral group Dic_3, whose class in H^2(S_3, F_2) = Z/2 is sg∪sg. The obstruction to lifting any φ: Γ_Q → S_3 over the character of Q(√−3) is therefore (−3,−3) = (−3,−1) ∈ Br_2(Q). This is nonzero, ramified at ∞ and at 3, so no lift exists, surjective or not. Already over R, complex conjugation maps to a transposition, which has no lift of order 2.

This conflicts with arithmetic reality. Curves y^2 = x^3 + b over Q have j = 0, and for b a cube their 2-torsion image is exactly a transposition subgroup, i.e. the case T that the page says cannot lift. So the model [U_{0,3}/S̃_3] with constant S̃_3 and this Galois structure is not the true Q-form of M_{1,1}. The S_3-action on the Legendre family needs √λ-type μ_2-twists. Likewise the claim on the previous page, that ordinary rational points of M'_{1,1} do not lift to M_{1,1}, holds only for the model and not for the actual Deligne–Mumford stack. This relies on my reading of his definitions, which are on other pages.

ideas.what: Presentation of M_{1,1} as a quotient of the λ-line by a central extension S̃_3 of S_3 by ±1 (binary dihedral, order 12), with the kernel over μ equal to Z/6
ideas.modern_name: Legendre presentation / orbifold quotient of the λ-line; SL(2,Z) modulo a free normal subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Klein); stacky form folklore (Deligne–Rapoport era)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z)^ but not this finite model explicitly

ideas.what: Rational points of the stack over a fixed point of the coarse space correspond to conjugacy classes of lifts of a Galois homomorphism through a finite group extension (torsor lifting)
ideas.modern_name: residual gerbes and twisted forms; points of quotient stacks as torsors; Galois embedding problems
ideas.where_published: related ideas in the Longue Marche and in the section-conjecture letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: Nonliftability of the section-induced torsor T through Z/4 because Q(√−3) is not a sum-of-two-squares field; reduction to the dihedral fields Q(ζ_3, ∛m)
ideas.modern_name: embedding problem with obstruction a quaternion algebra (Witt's criterion)

missed.claim: Grothendieck left the existence of lifts Γ_Q → S̃_3 (surjective onto S_3) as an unfinished 'class field theory exercise'. In his model the answer is negative: the obstruction is the quaternion algebra (−3,−1), nonzero at ∞ and 3. This shows his chosen Q-structure on M_{1,1} differs from the actual stack, where j = 0 curves over Q exist. The care needed with Galois twists of finite orbifold presentations, when matching rational points with sections, is well understood today.
missed.quote: un exercice plaisant et délectable de théorie des corps de classes (next page); ce torseur T n'a pas de relèvement par un T̃
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It illustrates the subtlety of Q-forms when testing the section conjecture at orbifold (stacky) points of M_{1,1}, a topic treated in later work on sections at points with extra automorphisms. Nothing here is beyond the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine torsor and embedding-problem analysis of rational points of M_{1,1} over j = 0 in a finite orbifold model. It is interesting mainly as a working document, and its conclusion appears to rest on a model whose Q-form differs from the true stack. There are no new results.
transcription_corrections: The Galois group is written Π_Q (Grothendieck's notation), not Γ_Q.
'des pts Q-rationnels o de E'' should read 'du pt Q-rationnel o de E''.
Previous page: 'Spec Q(√−1)' is very likely Spec Q(√−3) = Q(j), j a cube root of unity, consistent with 'sur K ⊃ Q(j), somme de deux pts'. 'Q(√3)' is likely Q(√−3).
The NB annotation '(canonique)' qualifies the map S̃_3 → μ.
